```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(readxl); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr); library(ggplot2)
```

# Purpose

Two derived datasets and a look at each:

1. **Binary** — did this participant report a visual pseudo-scotoma anywhere under this
   stimulus? One yes/no per participant x stimulus, collapsed across the 12 drawings.
2. **Count** — how many of the 12 drawings were affected? 0 to 12.

Descriptive only. No hypothesis is tested here.

# Colour decisions

Recorded because they are choices, not defaults.

**Binary: light neutral for absent, blue for present.** Not red/green. Red/green measures a
CVD separation of dE 7.2 under protanopia, which sits in the 6-8 warning band -- roughly one
man in twelve could not reliably tell the two states apart, on a figure whose entire job is
telling two states apart. Neutral vs blue measures dE 37.8 under the same simulation, and
separates on lightness as well as hue, so it survives greyscale printing too.

**Count: one blue hue, light to dark.** Never a rainbow. Zero is held out in the same neutral
as the binary figure, so "nothing happened" reads as nothing rather than as the bottom of a
scale.

The CSVs written below are the table view for both figures, so no value is reachable only by
colour.

```{r palette}
col_absent  <- "#f0efec"   # neutral - reads as "nothing"
col_present <- "#2a78d6"   # blue, categorical slot 1
ramp_blue   <- c("#cde2fb", "#9ec5f4", "#6da7ec", "#3987e5",
                 "#256abf", "#184f95", "#0d366b")
surface     <- "#fcfcfb"
ink_muted   <- "#898781"
ink_primary <- "#0b0b0b"
```

# Load and reshape

```{r load}
raw_dir <- file.path("..", "..", "data", "raw")
xl <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(xl) == 1)

# The workbook is often open in Excel, and then cannot be read in place by any ordinary
# route. readable_copy() falls through three of them; see src/readable_copy.R.
source("readable_copy.R")

d <- read_excel(readable_copy(xl), sheet = "Datos", skip = 1)
names(d)[1:4] <- c("row_index", "pid", "sex", "age")
grid_cols <- names(d)[5:ncol(d)]
stopifnot(length(grid_cols) == 23 * 12, all(unlist(d[grid_cols]) %in% c(0, 1)))
```

Stimulus labels, from the workbook's `Variables` sheet. `E1` is sound alone; `E2`-`E12` are
the eleven oral stimuli with sound; `E13`-`E23` are the same eleven without it.

```{r labels}
oral <- c("M1", "M2", "M3", "11V", "21V", "31V", "41V", "11P", "21P", "31L", "41L")

stim <- tibble(
  e     = 1:23,
  label = c("Sound", oral, oral),
  phase = factor(c("Sound alone", rep("Oral + sound", 11), rep("Oral alone", 11)),
                 levels = c("Sound alone", "Oral + sound", "Oral alone")),
  type  = c("Sound", rep(c(rep("COS", 3), rep("DS", 8)), 2))
)

long <- d |>
  select(pid, all_of(grid_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(-pid, names_to = "cell", values_to = "vs") |>
  mutate(im = as.integer(str_match(cell, "^IM(\\d+) ")[, 2]),
         e  = as.integer(str_match(cell, " E(\\d+)$")[, 2])) |>
  left_join(stim, by = "e")

stopifnot(nrow(long) == 38 * 23 * 12)
```

# The two matrices

```{r matrices}
by_stim <- long |>
  group_by(pid, e, label, phase, type) |>
  summarise(n_vs = sum(vs), any_vs = as.integer(n_vs > 0), .groups = "drop")

# Wide, one row per participant, for reading in Excel
col_names <- paste0("E", stim$e, "_", str_replace_all(stim$label, " ", "_"),
                    ifelse(stim$phase == "Oral + sound" , "_snd", ""))

to_wide <- function(value_col) {
  by_stim |>
    select(pid, e, val = all_of(value_col)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = e, values_from = val, names_sort = TRUE) |>
    rename_with(~ col_names, .cols = -pid) |>
    arrange(pid)
}

vs_binary <- to_wide("any_vs")
vs_count  <- to_wide("n_vs")

proc <- file.path("..", "..", "data", "processed")
dir.create(proc, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(vs_binary, file.path(proc, "vs_binary_participant_by_stimulus.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(vs_count,  file.path(proc, "vs_count_participant_by_stimulus.csv"),  row.names = FALSE)

cat("binary:", nrow(vs_binary), "x", ncol(vs_binary), " count:",
    nrow(vs_count), "x", ncol(vs_count), "\n")
cat("total stimulus-level VS:", sum(by_stim$any_vs), "of", nrow(by_stim), "\n")
cat("count range:", min(by_stim$n_vs), "-", max(by_stim$n_vs), "\n")
```

```{r peek}
knitr::kable(vs_binary[1:5, 1:8], caption = "Binary matrix, first 5 participants")
knitr::kable(vs_count[1:5, 1:8],  caption = "Count matrix, first 5 participants")
```

# Heatmaps

Row order is a choice, so it is a parameter of this file rather than a second copy of it.

| `sort_participants` | Order |
|---|---|
| `"sound"` (default) | drawings affected under **sound alone**, then **how many of the 11 oral + sound stimuli were a yes**, both descending |
| `"burden"` | total affected drawings across all 23 stimuli |
| `"id"` | original participant ID |

The secondary key counts *stimuli*, not drawings — "more oral yes than no" is a question about
how many of the eleven responded, and a participant with one stimulus affecting many drawings
is a different case from one with many stimuli affecting one drawing each. The two rank
participants differently (they correlate 0.81). Only 7 distinct sound values occur among the
23 responders, so the secondary key breaks 16 of those 23 rows and is doing real work.

The default groups the sound-responders into a block at the top — the subgroup the
elimination endpoint is about — so the elimination pattern can be read by scanning right from
the sound column into "Oral + sound" and seeing where cells turn grey. IDs stay on the axis
under every option, so nothing is hidden, and the caption records which order was used.

```{r order}
blocks <- by_stim |>
  mutate(block = case_when(e == 1 ~ "sound", e %in% 2:12 ~ "oral_snd", TRUE ~ "oral")) |>
  group_by(pid, block) |>
  summarise(draws = sum(n_vs),     # drawings affected in this block
            yes   = sum(any_vs),   # stimuli in this block that produced any VS
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = block, values_from = c(draws, yes)) |>
  mutate(total = draws_sound + draws_oral_snd + draws_oral)

ord <- switch(params$sort_participants,
  sound  = arrange(blocks, desc(draws_sound), desc(yes_oral_snd)),
  burden = arrange(blocks, desc(total)),
  id     = arrange(blocks, pid),
  stop("sort_participants must be 'sound', 'burden' or 'id'")
)

by_stim <- by_stim |>
  mutate(pid_f   = factor(pid, levels = rev(ord$pid)),
         label_f = factor(label, levels = c("Sound", oral)))

sort_note <- switch(params$sort_participants,
  sound  = "Participants ordered by drawings affected under sound alone, then by how many of the 11 oral + sound stimuli produced a pseudo-scotoma.",
  burden = "Participants ordered by total affected drawings, most affected at top.",
  id     = "Participants in original ID order."
)

cat("sound-responders in the top block:", sum(blocks$draws_sound > 0), "of", nrow(blocks), "\n")
cat("oral + sound 'yes' count, range:", range(blocks$yes_oral_snd), "of 11\n")
```

```{r theme}
theme_heat <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(16, "pt"),
    # The "Sound alone" panel is one column wide, so its centred strip label
    # is wider than the panel and gets clipped to "und alo". Let it overflow
    # into the panel gap instead.
    strip.clip      = "off",
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, colour = ink_muted),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = ink_muted),
    axis.title      = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 9),
    strip.text      = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 9),
    plot.title      = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 9),
    plot.caption    = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 7.5, hjust = 0),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = surface, colour = NA),
    legend.title    = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8.5),
    legend.text     = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8)
  )

# Tile borders drawn in the surface colour ARE the 2px gap between marks,
# not a border around them.
gap <- 0.35
```

```{r figure-dir}
fig <- file.path("..", "outputs", "figures")
dir.create(fig, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Binary — all three phases

Rebuilt 2026-08-18 for the client summary, which needs one figure showing where a
pseudo-scotoma was reported across **all** three measured phases. It carries no
classification: every cell is the same yes/no question, so sound alone, sound + oral and oral
alone are read on one scale.

This is a different figure from the two in `collapse_conditions_and_classify.Rmd` and writes a
different filename, so neither overwrites the other:

- `heatmap_elimination.png` — the 23 sound-responders only, sound + oral cells scored as
  eliminated or not. That is the endpoint figure.
- `heatmap_oral_alone_vs.png` — the oral-alone phase on its own.
- **this figure** — all 38 participants, all 23 conditions, presence only.

⚠️ **Prevalence is read down a column, never across a row.** The middle panel holds eleven
conditions and the right panel eleven more, against the left panel's one, so counting how much
blue a panel contains compares opportunity counts rather than stimuli.

```{r heatmap-binary, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, dpi=300}
# Manuscript wording for the panel headings. The internal `phase` levels are left alone -- the
# prevalence barchart below filters on them by name.
heat_bin <- by_stim |>
  mutate(
    state   = if_else(any_vs == 1, "Pseudo-scotoma", "None"),
    phase_f = factor(c("Sound alone" = "Sound alone", "Oral + sound" = "Sound + OPS",
                       "Oral alone" = "OPS only")[as.character(phase)],
                     levels = c("Sound alone", "Sound + OPS", "OPS only"))
  )
stopifnot(!any(is.na(heat_bin$phase_f)))

phase_n <- heat_bin |>
  group_by(phase_f) |>
  summarise(k = n_distinct(pid[any_vs == 1]), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(phase_n$k == c(23, 34, 31))

p_bin <- ggplot(heat_bin, aes(label_f, pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  facet_grid(. ~ phase_f, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Pseudo-scotoma" = col_present, "None" = col_absent),
                    breaks = "Pseudo-scotoma") +
  labs(
    title    = "Visual pseudo-scotomas by participant and stimulus condition",
    subtitle = paste0("One cell per participant per condition, collapsed across the 12 ",
                      "drawings (n = 38). Sound alone 23/38;\nat least one sound + OPS ",
                      "condition 34/38; at least one OPS condition without sound 31/38."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "OPS = oral proprioceptive stimuli. M1-M3 are combined oral stimuli; the remaining ",
      "eight are dental stimuli, labelled by tooth (FDI notation)\n",
      "and site (V = buccal, P = palatal, L = lingual). ",
      "Prevalence is read down a column: each column is one condition with one opportunity\n",
      "for a pseudo-scotoma to be recorded, so the columns are directly comparable, whereas ",
      "the sound + OPS and OPS only panels contain eleven\n",
      "conditions each against the single sound condition. The OPS only phase was always ",
      "performed last, so differences between phases are\n",
      "confounded with time, fatigue and practice. Descriptive; no intervals and no test."
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
p_bin

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_vs_binary_three_phases.png"), p_bin,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

## Count — how many of the 12 drawings

```{r heatmap-count, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, dpi=300}
p_cnt <- ggplot(by_stim, aes(label_f, pid_f,
                             fill = ifelse(n_vs == 0, NA_real_, n_vs))) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  facet_grid(. ~ phase, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours  = ramp_blue,
    limits   = c(1, 12),
    breaks   = c(1, 3, 6, 9, 12),
    na.value = col_absent,
    name     = "Drawings\naffected",
    guide    = guide_colourbar(barwidth = 0.6, barheight = 7, ticks = FALSE)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Number of drawings affected, by participant and stimulus",
    subtitle = "0 to 12. Grey = no pseudo-scotoma under that stimulus",
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption  = paste0(sort_note, "\n",
                      "n = 38. Values in data/processed/vs_count_participant_by_stimulus.csv")
  ) +
  theme_heat
p_cnt

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_vs_count.png"), p_cnt,
       width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

# Prevalence by condition

`vs_prevalence_barchart.png` existed in `outputs/figures/` with **no script anywhere in the
repository that produced it** — found orphaned on 2026-08-17. It is rebuilt here so it has a
source of truth, and rebuilt to Esther's specification: **the sound-only condition and the
oral-only conditions, with the sound + oral conditions excluded.**

⚠️ **One bar per condition, not one bar per phase.** The eleven oral-alone stimuli are shown
individually rather than collapsed into a single "any oral stimulus" bar. A collapsed bar would
have eleven chances to be positive against the sound bar's one, so it would measure the number
of opportunities rather than the effect of the stimulus — which is exactly why
`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` §5 declines Cochran's Q across phases. Every bar here is one condition,
twelve drawings, one opportunity, so the bars are like-for-like.

No confidence intervals: these are descriptive. Wilson intervals for every proportion that
enters a comparison are analysis 2 of the plan, and the plan is not yet agreed.

```{r prevalence-barchart, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5, dpi=300}
prev_dat <- by_stim |>
  filter(phase != "Oral + sound") |>
  group_by(label, phase) |>
  summarise(n_vs = sum(any_vs), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    pct    = 100 * n_vs / n_distinct(by_stim$pid),
    group  = factor(if_else(phase == "Sound alone", "Sound alone",
                            "Oral stimulus alone, no sound"),
                    levels = c("Sound alone", "Oral stimulus alone, no sound")),
    lab_f  = factor(label, levels = c("Sound", oral))
  )

n_p <- n_distinct(by_stim$pid)

p_prev <- ggplot(prev_dat, aes(lab_f, pct)) +
  # One measure, one hue. The two condition types are separated by panel rather than by
  # colour, so no colour is spent re-encoding what the panel heading already says.
  geom_col(fill = col_present, width = 0.68) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_vs, "\n", round(pct), "%")),
            vjust = -0.25, size = 2.7, colour = ink_muted, lineheight = 0.95) +
  facet_grid(. ~ group, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  # Zero baseline, as a bar chart requires. The ceiling is 70 rather than 100 only because
  # nothing reaches 62% and the empty upper third made the bars harder to compare; no bar is
  # clipped and no difference is exaggerated.
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 70), breaks = seq(0, 70, 10),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.10))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Pseudo-scotoma prevalence, by condition",
    subtitle = paste0("Percentage of participants reporting a visual pseudo-scotoma in at ",
                      "least one of the 12 drawings. n = ", n_p, ".\nSound + oral conditions ",
                      "are excluded by design; see the caption."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participants with a pseudo-scotoma (%)",
    caption = paste0(
      "Counts above each bar are the number of participants, out of ", n_p, ".\n",
      "Each bar is a single condition with a single opportunity to be positive, so the bars ",
      "are directly comparable to each other. The eleven oral\n",
      "stimuli are NOT collapsed into one bar: a union over eleven conditions would have ",
      "eleven chances against the sound bar's one.\n",
      "Descriptive; no intervals and no test. The oral-alone phase always ran last, so ",
      "condition is confounded with time (ANALYSIS_PLAN.md 2a.1).\n",
      "Values in data/processed/vs_binary_participant_by_stimulus.csv"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "#e8e6e2", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(16, "pt"),
    strip.clip         = "off",
    strip.text         = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 9),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, colour = ink_muted),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(colour = ink_muted),
    axis.title         = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 9),
    plot.title         = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8.5),
    plot.caption       = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 7, hjust = 0),
    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = surface, colour = NA)
  )
p_prev

ggsave(file.path(fig, "vs_prevalence_barchart.png"), p_prev,
       width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```
